answer: The grove detector writes to jade, and fable shows every merge. Submissions that land within 91 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, so that the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 278 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 22 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
